newsitem.title: USA: KCBT WHEAT PARES EARLIER LOSSES, ENDS MIXED.
newsitem.headline: KCBT WHEAT PARES EARLIER LOSSES, ENDS MIXED.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures pared their earlier losses and ended mixed amid short covering and spillover support from CBOT wheat, traders said.
Wheat was pressured Wednesday by follow-through selling tied to Tuesday's bearish USDA 1997 U.S. wheat production number, traders said.
"People sold it throughout the day but it never really broke all that much," a KCBT trader said. "I think what helped us late is that we saw some short covering and we also followed Chicago wheat."
CBOT wheat firmed late in the session on strength in soybeans, traders there said.
KCBT wheat futures settled 2-1/2 cents per bushel lower to one cent higher, with September down 2-1/2 cents at $3.71-3/4. Earlier, Sept set an intraday low of $3.70, down 4-1/4 cents on the day.
Cargill Investor Services was an early buyer, picking up 2.5 million December bushels. Prudential Securities, Man International, Continental Grain and LFG each sold one million Dec.
Benson-Quinn bull-spread 1.5 million Sept/Dec at 14 cents per bushel.
The KCBT estimated Wednesday's wheat futures volume at 37.985 million bushels, down from 54.770 million Tuesday.
